claim_verdicts.evidence: Pinned docs support the per-dependent half: "The Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) ...: Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." (options.md:12). No pinned doc states "many small, focused interfaces beat one large one"; grep "segregat" in refs/dotnet-docs finds only this line and a bare list item. The ranking is unconditional and conflicts with the lesson's own section 6 ("a small count is a symptom, not the goal").
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) — no code should be forced to depend on methods it does not use; when different users need different parts of an interface, split it into small, focused interfaces instead of one large one.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." (interfaces.md:86). CS0535 fix: "Provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface, or declare the type as abstract" (interface-implementation-errors.md:140). Lesson text "C# requires a class to provide every member of an interface it implements" drops the default-implementation exception; true for the hypothetical's body-less members.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: On the implementing side, C# requires a class to provide every method the interface declares without a body of its own, which is all four here.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution (SDK 10, net10.0, scratchpad): interface with SendSms and GetDeliveryReport(int, bool); implementer still has GetDeliveryReport(int). Build: "error CS0535: 'Sms' does not implement interface member 'IChannel.GetDeliveryReport(int, bool)'". Doc: "The class must provide an implementation for every member declared in the interface" (interfaces.md:35). Holds for members without a default body, as in the lesson.
git show stage-0:.../INotifier.cs lines 5-8: `public interface INotifier { void Send(int orderId, string subject); }` - one member. Code block lines=5-8 matches character-for-character.

git show stage-0: line 5 `public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier`; line 7 private `List<string> sent`; line 9 `IReadOnlyList<string> Sent => sent`; lines 11-16 Send calls Format, sent.Add, Console.WriteLine; line 18 `protected abstract string Format(...)`; lines 21-31 EmailNotifier/SmsNotifier override only Format. Code block lines=21-31 matches.
`git -C examples/don-hang grep -n -i deliver stage-0 -- samples` returns no lines (exit 1). No INotificationChannel or GetDeliveryReport anywhere at stage-0.

"C# doesn't have the concept of checked exceptions. Any method might (in theory) throw any exception." (tips-for-java-developers.md:16) - nothing in the interface signature tells a caller that one implementation throws, so the caller cannot know from the type. The LSP link restates the prerequisite lesson.

Design judgement restating outline misconception 2, not a factual claim about a version. Consistent with the pinned framing of ISP per dependent ("depend only on the configuration settings that they use", options.md:12), which says nothing about member count.

issues.text: Unlisted claim about the samples, and false as a description of them: at stage-0 no code asks for an INotifier. `git grep -n INotifier stage-0` lists only INotifier.cs:5 and NotifierBase.cs:5; nothing outside Samples/Oop mentions Notifier. It also previews the DIP lesson's outline item 2 (code that takes an INotifier).
issues.quote: Code that needs to send something asks for an `INotifier` and can be given either one.
issues.fix: Replace with a sentence true of the code: "Both are `INotifier`s, so either one can be used wherever an `INotifier` is expected." and add it to claims (kind fact, source NotifierBase.cs:5,21,27). Do not describe a consumer that does not exist.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, too strong for callers. Probe (SDK 10): changing GetDeliveryReport's parameters gave CS0535 on the implementer only; a caller that calls only SendSms compiled unchanged. Same wording recurs in section 6 misconception 1 and in quiz q2 correct explanation ("a change to any of them can reach it").
issues.quote: a change to any method of that interface can reach that code.
issues.fix: Section 3: "code depends on an interface when it implements it or calls through it; an implementer must change when any method of the interface changes." Section 6: replace "still has to live with changes to the other three" with "still gets channels whose other three methods may be filler". q2 correct: "...still depends on the other three, which may be filler that throws." Add the claim to meta.

issues.text: Claim 2 rephrased: C# exempts interface members that have a default implementation (interfaces.md:86). The absolute form is also repeated in quiz q1 correct explanation ("C# requires every member of the interface").
issues.quote: C# requires a class to provide every member of an interface it implements.
issues.fix: Use claim 2 suggested_text in section 4; in q1 explanation write "C# requires every method the interface declares without a body, so `SmsNotifier` would need filler for..." (en and vi).

issues.text: Unconditional ranking with no pinned source; contradicts section 6 which says count is not the goal and a three-method interface is fine when all users need all three.
issues.quote: many small, focused interfaces beat one large one.
issues.fix: Use claim 1 suggested_text: add the condition "when different users need different parts of an interface, split it into small, focused interfaces".

issues.text: The arrows mean two different things: F --> S is 'implemented by', F --> C is 'used by', and I --> E / I --> M skip NotifierBase. The section 4 prose never mentions EmailNotifier or SmsNotifier under INotifier; I only learn how they relate in section 5. I cannot narrate the right half of the diagram after reading section 4.
issues.fix: In the third paragraph of section 4, add one sentence: "On the right of the diagram, EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier each implement INotifier (through NotifierBase) and have real behaviour for its one method." Also add one clause saying the left arrows show who implements and who calls the fat interface.

issues.text: The paragraph is announced as the calling side, but its concrete consequence (a GetDeliveryReport change forces SmsNotifier to change) is about implementers. I cannot see what actually goes wrong for the confirmation code, and I half-conclude the confirmation code must change too. The caller-side harm only appears later, in section 6.
issues.quote: If someone changes the parameters of `GetDeliveryReport`, every class that implements the interface has to change, including `SmsNotifier`
issues.fix: Move the GetDeliveryReport sentence to the implementing-side paragraph, and give the calling-side paragraph its own concrete cost, e.g. one sentence: a class that only sends SMS cannot be passed to the confirmation code unless it adds filler for the other three.

issues.text: The misconception as written can be read as 'every implementing class uses every method', which would not be a fat interface at all, so the belief seems harmless and I cannot see what is wrong with it. Quiz q2 states the intended belief more clearly ('each of its methods is used by some class in the system').
issues.quote: A big interface is fine as long as every class implementing it eventually uses every method somewhere.
issues.fix: Reword the belief to match q2: "A big interface is fine as long as each of its methods is used by some class somewhere in the system."

issues.text: 'without a body of its own' made me stop: the five-line summaries only say an interface says what callers may call, so an interface method having a body is a new idea here. I re-read the sentence twice. Same phrase in q1's correct explanation ('without a default body').
issues.quote: C# requires a class to provide every method the interface declares without a body of its own, which is all four here.
issues.fix: Add a short reminder in the same sentence: "(C# lets an interface give a method a default body; none of these four has one)".

issues.text: 'The code that sends an order confirmation' is used throughout (diagram, try it, quiz) but never tied to anything in the samples. I know PlaceOrderSplit.Notify from earlier lessons and cannot tell whether this is it or a hypothetical.
issues.quote: And the code that sends an order confirmation calls only one of the four, yet now depends on all of them.
issues.fix: Add a few words saying whether this is PlaceOrderSplit.Notify or an imagined piece of code, e.g. "the code that sends an order confirmation (imagined for this lesson)".

issues.text: 'users' could mean people using the app; here it means code that calls or implements the interface. I had to check which one.
issues.quote: ISP's answer is to cut interfaces along what their users need.
issues.fix: Replace "their users" with "the code that calls or implements them".

issues.text: q2: correct option c is nearly a verbatim sentence from section 6 ('ISP asks about each piece of code that depends on the interface, not about the system as a whole'), so it can be matched without understanding.
issues.quote: False, because ISP asks about each caller and implementer, not the system as a whole.
issues.fix: Rephrase option c in new words, e.g. "False, because the confirmation code still needs channels that carry all four methods, even if other code uses them."

issues.text: q4: correct option a is the longest and the only one using the lesson's term 'fat interface'; I can pick it from wording alone.
issues.quote: The fat interface forced `SmsNotifier` to promise `SendEmail`, which it could only fill with a throw.
issues.fix: Shorten option a to similar length as the others and drop the term, e.g. "The interface made `SmsNotifier` promise an email it cannot send."

issues.text: q6: the blank is filled by copying the Core concepts sentence word for word; it tests recall of wording, not understanding.
issues.quote: ISP: no code should be forced to depend on methods it does not ____.
issues.fix: Blank a word that needs understanding, e.g. "When SmsNotifier must write bodies for SendEmail and SendPush, those bodies are called ____." (answer: filler).
